newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Fertilizer Industries yr pre-tax profit up.
newsitem.headline: Irish Fertilizer Industries yr pre-tax profit up.

text.p: Irish Fertilizer Industries (IFI) said on Wednesday that it made pre-tax profits of 18.7 million Irish pounds after restructuring costs of 1.7 million in the year to September 30, 1996.
This was up from pre-tax profit of 18.4 million in 1995.
But turnover slipped to 161.5 million from 165.6 million a year earlier because of a general fall of five percent in the market for agricultural fertilizers, IFI said in a statement.
"While sales were relatively buoyant in the early part of the year, volumes fell noticeably in the second half due to a combination of factors in the agricultural industry," IFI said.
Operating profits slipped to 19.8 million from 20.0 million but operating margins rose to 12.3 percent from 12.1 percent while net margins increased to 11.6 percent from 11.1 percent.

The company said it invested a total of 13 million Irish pounds in new capital expenditure during the year, improving operating efficiencies and environmental performance at its production facilities in Cork, Arklow and Belfast.
Managing director Tom Jago said the company's financial performance was particularly pleasing considering the high level of investment undertaken.

"While the fertilizer industry remains somewhat volatile, our strong financial position means we can confidently plan to consolidate our position both in Ireland and in the European industry," he said.
Net borrowings at year-end were 200,000 punts while the group's balance sheet showed shareholders' funds rising to 67.5 million from 56.2 million.
